# Work Context CLI

<!-- Generated by go run ./tools/clisurface -write-doc. Do not edit by hand. -->

[Back to CLI Surface SSOT](../cli-surface.md)

The work-context commands let an agent running under the daemon, or a person in a terminal, read the Riido context of a work item on demand instead of receiving everything in the prompt. They extend this binary; there is no separate CLI engine.

Two modes share the same commands and output contract:

- agent mode: selected when the daemon injected `RIIDO_RUN_TOKEN` into the runtime process. Calls go CLI → local IPC (daemon broker, `RIIDO_DAEMON_SOCKET` or the default agentd endpoint) → control-plane run grant → monolith. The agent never holds a user credential
- user mode: selected otherwise. Calls go straight to Riido servers with the signed-in user's OAuth credential kept in the OS keychain behind a user-presence check. The daemon is not involved

Mode selection is not a security boundary. A shell-capable agent can unset environment variables; protection comes from server-side permission checks and from the OS refusing to release the user credential without user presence.

Current availability in this binary:

- available: `riido capabilities`, `riido doctor`, `riido auth status`, `riido auth logout`, and argument validation for every work-context command
- agent-mode reads (`work`, `context`, `whoami`) send the `context_read` IPC request. A daemon without the broker, or with `RIIDO_CONTEXT_CLI` off, answers `unknown method`, which maps to exit 8 `CONTEXT_READ_UNSUPPORTED`
- with `RIIDO_CONTEXT_CLI=on`, the daemon issues a random per-run capability at provider launch (stored only as a SHA-256 hash, rotated on retry) and injects `RIIDO_RUN_TOKEN`, `RIIDO_DAEMON_SOCKET`, `RIIDO_TASK_ID`, `RIIDO_WORKSPACE_ID`, and its own bin directory first on `PATH`
- the broker rejects missing, unknown, rotated, or ended-run capabilities with exit 4 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, and task or workspace mismatches with exit 4 `OUT_OF_RUN_SCOPE`. It answers `whoami` with run facts plus a `REQUESTER_UNRESOLVED` warning
- on the SaaS control plane, Riido data reads come from the assignment context snapshot (control-plane ADR-001 option 4): the task context the server composed into the prompt at assign/reply time. The broker sends `POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/assignment-context` with the device credential and the run's lease token, which never leave the daemon. `context get` (without `--work` it reads the assigned task), `work get` (the task or its project, milestone, or parent), `work tree`, `work relations` (links, files, and related work and meeting titles), and `work comments` (all comments stored at assignment time in priority order — the comment that started the run, the 20 most recent, then older — paged by `--cursor`) are served with an `ASSIGNMENT_SNAPSHOT` warning. `--budget CHARS` is enforced by the broker: the longest free-text fields (content, body, description, summary) are halved (marked `…`) while ids, keys and URLs are never shortened, until the JSON data fits, with a `BUDGET_TRUNCATED` warning and truncated sources, or `BUDGET_EXCEEDED` when the structure alone is larger. A run whose runtime cannot answer the activity check in time gets a retryable exit 6 and keeps its capability; the server records each served source as a read. `agents list` (50 per `--cursor` page) and `agents show <agent-id>` are not snapshot reads: the control-plane answers them live (`live: true`) for the requester-visible agents only, with public description and role status, work status, runtime connection and `callable`/`unavailable_reasons` but no instructions or owners, and the broker marks them with a `LIVE_STATUS` warning instead of `ASSIGNMENT_SNAPSHOT`. Work outside the snapshot returns exit 4 `OUT_OF_RUN_SCOPE`, an ended run exit 10 `LEASE_LOST`, and a server without the feature exit 8 `CONTROL_PLANE_UNSUPPORTED`
- `work activity`, `work search`, and `context changes` are not part of the snapshot and return exit 8 `CONTROL_PLANE_UNSUPPORTED`; file and task-DB control planes have no snapshot either
- Capability-bearing provider launches add snapshot CLI instructions on the existing native/inline surfaces. Claude approval mode adds only the supported read leaves to --allowedTools: context get, work get/tree/relations/comments, agents list/show and meeting list/get, with exact and argument-bearing rules. No broad riido/work/context wildcard, write, auth, unsupported read, or permission-bypass rule is added. Caller allowedTools aliases cannot override the daemon-owned list while enabled. Missing capability/socket/task keeps prior launch behavior. Native shell composition parsing remains Claude-owned and needs real-runtime QA. Codex uses a daemon-owned, shell-quoted absolute executable in its CLI instructions to avoid login-shell PATH replacement; this does not change native sandbox/socket permissions.
- user-mode reads and `auth login` return exit 8 `USER_MODE_UNAVAILABLE` until the server auth contract (ADR) and keychain storage land

Output contract (envelope v1): with `--json`, stdout carries exactly one JSON object `{schema_version, request_id, data, sources, warnings, page, error}`; progress and diagnostics go to stderr. `error` is `{code, message, retryable, next_action, request_id}` and never contains tokens or response headers.

Local context-read audit lines identify the requested target: `agents show` records its agent ID, `meeting get` records its meeting ID, work/context and meeting-list reads record an explicit work ID, and commands without a target record `-`. Command and target remain quoted on one line. Run capabilities, lease credentials and response bodies are never included.

Meeting reads use the same run capability, lease, snapshot warning, envelope and budget. `meeting list [--work <RIID-1234|ID>] [--budget CHARS]` selects the assigned work by default and returns only connected meeting metadata and body_status, never document content. `meeting get <MEETING-ID> [--budget CHARS]` returns the captured meeting document, including an authoritative empty body or a partial body marked truncated. The control-plane wire uses existing view/target fields with views meetings/meeting. Meeting bodies are assignment-time snapshots, not live reads. Outside-snapshot meetings, captured permission denials, deleted bodies and collection failures retain OUT_OF_RUN_SCOPE, PERMISSION_DENIED, NOT_FOUND and UNAVAILABLE respectively. Older snapshots without captured bodies never imply an empty document. Board data, comments and linked-work expansion are not included in a meeting document read. Claude approval mode adds only the two exact meeting read leaves and their argument-bearing rules; no meeting wildcard or write rule is allowed.

Exit codes:

- 0 success (including accepted queued work)
- 2 usage error, including secrets passed as arguments
- 3 authentication required or expired
- 4 permission denied
- 5 not found (including expired snapshots)
- 6 connection, timeout, or transient server failure
- 7 rate limited
- 8 unsupported version, connection, or format
- 9 incomplete result (partial data kept with warnings)
- 10 conflict (version mismatch, session in use, lease lost)

Secrets never travel in argv. `--token`, `--secret`, `--password`, `--api-key` and their `--flag=value` forms are rejected with exit 2 on every work-context command; `riido auth login --with-token` reads stdin only.

The envelope and exit codes are provisional in `internal/contextcli`. They must move to `riido-contracts` before Riido Desktop or control-plane consume them.

QA reproduction tools are preserved in `scripts/riido-cli-qa/` and require Python 3.9 or newer with only the standard library. From the repository root, run `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/riido-cli-qa -p 'test_*.py' -v` for the offline fixtures, and `python3 scripts/riido-cli-qa/staging_probe.py` for the offline NOT_RUN report. Neither command contacts a daemon, server, or provider.

`staging_probe.py --execute` is only for an already approved staging Agent run with daemon-injected capability/socket/task environment. `--help` lists the required non-secret approval reference, approved daemon build and CLI SHA-256, assigned work, in-snapshot parent, outside-snapshot work, and comment fixture count. The operator must independently verify the running daemon endpoint/build: the probe checks only the CLI binary on PATH. Do not copy credentials into arguments, files, or logs. The probe does not install, authenticate, dispatch an Agent, deploy, or grant approval; successful reads add server audit records, stop at the first failed check, and are not retried.

Every probe report keeps `staging_acceptance=NOT_COMPLETE` and manual checks at `NOT_RUN`. Offline fixtures, local socket/provider checks, actual server authentication and lease checks, Desktop installation, SSE visibility, and retention acceptance remain separate evidence. Automated PASS alone is not staging or release approval.

Ended-run capability QA uses `python3 scripts/riido-cli-qa/ended_run_probe.py watch` (offline by default). For an approved run, an operator starts `watch --execute` outside the Agent process tree with the approved CLI path/hash, exact daemon socket, expected task, approval/build references, environment and timeout from `--help`. Its handoff socket must be inside an owned canonical mode-0700 directory. After READY, the Agent runs `python3 /absolute/repo/scripts/riido-cli-qa/ended_run_probe.py send --handoff /private/socket/path`. No token argument is accepted: the sender inherits only its existing run environment and transfers the capability over a mode-0600 Unix socket; both peers verify the same OS user. Core dumps are disabled. The token remains in memory, local IPC and the CLI child environment, never a file or report.

The observer first proves the capability works with `whoami` and matches the exact active execution. It then observes both execution ownership and the native slot absent twice on the same daemon PID/start time/version before invoking `whoami` and `context get` once each with that same capability. The local-only `whoami` rejection rules out a server-side permission denial masquerading as broker revocation. Both calls must return CLI exit 4, PERMISSION_DENIED and no data/sources; a daemon restart, inconclusive status, timeout, reappearing execution or another error is a failure. Socket reads and the overall watcher have absolute time limits, so partial byte trickles cannot extend the budget. This proves local ended-run rejection, not the separate control-plane stale-lease path (exit 10), server terminal persistence, or release acceptance. It never dispatches, cancels, restarts or replaces a daemon; use the external watcher so provider process cleanup cannot terminate the observer.
